recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for FHIR core. No core follow-up is indicated; future changes to these extension definitions, contexts, bindings, names, or search parameters should be handled in the FHIR Extension Pack after the responsible work group resolves a FHIR-extensions issue.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive with Modification Patient Care issue for R5 requesting support for barriers and supportive/protective factors on request-type resources and Goal. The approved resolution specified workflow-barrier and workflow-protectiveFactor as 0..* CodeableReference extensions, example bindings, Reference(Any), and contexts Goal, CommunicationRequest, and CarePlan.activity.
initial_application: FHIR core commit e547441b507bf3733608ce11ecb92a5a62f50a3d added J#36415 workflow extension spreadsheet rows and valueset-barrier/valueset-protective-factor source files. The current core checkout no longer carries those extension definitions because dd468d4f1799dd79819315b211588ef1cf4586e0 removed extension artifacts from R5 core source; core retains only OID registrations for the relevant canonical URLs.
additional_context: The FHIR Extension Pack checkout contains the authoritative current StructureDefinition and ValueSet files for workflow-barrier and workflow-protectiveFactor. FHIR-36691, the same-change-family SearchParameter request, is already represented on the combined branch as an external-repo audit; FHIR-40301 later repeated that SearchParameter request under FHIR-extensions. FHIR-44354 is a later Triaged/unresolved context/naming request and does not change the applied FHIR-36415 scope.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit on the combined branch. No core source was changed because re-adding these extension definitions to core would duplicate artifacts now maintained in HL7/fhir-extensions.
